text:
The UN in Moldova
THE UNITED NATIONS 
DEVELOPMENT ASSISTANCE FRAMEWORK
Republic of Moldova
February 2001
TABLE OF CONTENTS
Executive Summary
Purpose. The United Nations Development Assistance Framework (UNDAF) seeks to provide a coherent and coordinated strategy for assistance from the UN system to Moldova for the period 2001-2005.  It will support the achievement of the objectives of the Action Program of the Government.  
Goals.  The three UNDAF goals for Moldova are:
· 	A vibrant market economy that will create sustainable livelihoods;
· 	Governance that is effective and accountable at both the central and local levels;
· 	Social services in health, education and social welfare that are provided effectively and fairly to meet the needs of the general population and of the vulnerable groups in particular.
In seeking to achieve these goals, the UNDAF will also integrate four other issues that crosscut all three goals:  poverty alleviation, sustainable development, gender equality and human rights.
Objectives.  The UNDAF sets out objectives for the UN system for each of the three goals as follows:
1.  Economic Growth and Reform.  The UN system will provide advice to the Government and strengthen its capacity to implement appropriate policies and programmes for sustainable economic growth and stability, further reform of the economy, job creation, and the promotion of trade, investment and regional economic cooperation.
Under this objective, the UN system will provide assistance in the following areas:
Macro-economic, fiscal and monetary policies for growth and stability;
Banking sector reform and development;
Privatization and promotion of foreign direct investment;
Sustainable development of agriculture and industry;
Income generating activities;
Trade and regional economic cooperation;
Infrastructure for development.
2.  Governance.  The UN system will advise the Government, strengthen its capacity to develop appropriate policies and support the implementation of concrete programmes aimed at the implementation of the public sector reform, increasing capacities of local administrations to manage development processes at the local level, strengthening the judiciary, promotion of human rights and the implementation of conventions and laws ratified by Moldova over the years of independence. The UN system will also provide direct support to refugees and internally displaced persons in Moldova, promote the culture of peace, and facilitate the development of civil society.
Under this objective, the UN system will provide assistance in the following areas:
Public sector reform;
Decentralization and strengthening of local government;
Gender issues in governance;
Combating corruption and drug trafficking;
Implementation of environmental conventions and laws;
Judicial reform;
Strengthening the Center for Human Rights;
Promotion of civil society organizations;
Promotion of the culture of peace and conflict mitigation.
3.  Social Sector Reform and Development.  The UN system will advise the Government and strengthen its capacity to develop and implement policies and programmes for reform and restructuring in education and culture, health, and services for vulnerable groups. The UN system will also support the development and strengthening of the data collection and analysis in the priority areas. 
Under this objective, the UN system will provide assistance in the following areas:
Reform, restructuring, capacity building and service delivery in education and culture;
Reform, restructuring, capacity building and service delivery in health;
Reform, restructuring, capacity building and service delivery in services for vulnerable groups;
Data collection on human development and poverty and related capacity building for data analysis.
Cooperation Strategies.  To achieve these objectives, the cooperation strategies for the UN system will include a mixture of advocacy; policy advice; creation, transformation or strengthening of institutional capacity; provision of the investment and balance of payments loans; and in some cases, direct support for the provision of essential services.
Opportunities for enhanced collaboration within the UN system and with other development partners are identified in such areas as income generation, private sector development, strengthening local government, promotion of gender equality, combating corruption and drug trafficking, and education.
Review.  The UNDAF will be monitored and reviewed regularly by the UN Resident Coordinator with the UN Agency representatives in Moldova and by the Government.
Programme Resources.  The estimated total of regular and other programme resources to be provided to Moldova by the UN system for the five year period is $27,810,000, excluding loans and related assistance provided by the international financial institutions of the UN system.
I.	Rationale for the UN Development Assistance Framework
Country Context.  In the past few years, Moldova has gone from being characterized as “a model of correct reforms, a perfect laboratory for their implementation” (Economist, March, 1995) to one of the poorest countries in Europe with a host of economic and social problems.  Moldova’s reforms and economic management during 1992-95 were highly successful, but momentum was lost in the middle years of the 1990s when the reforms were not sufficiently widened and deepened.  In 1998, the country was hard hit when Russia, its most important trading partner, suffered a major financial crisis.  Since then, privatization, exports and foreign direct investment have all slowed and Moldova’s rapidly growing external debt is raising concern about the country’s financial stability. 
Public confidence in the government, which is seen by the population as corrupt, is low. The country also continues to bear the social, economic and psychological burdens of the unresolved conflict in the breakaway Transnistrian area. During 1999-2000 the situation was further complicated by political instability as the country had three governments during an 18-month period.  
In the social sector, health, education and other social services are breaking down due to lack of funding.  Drug use, HIV/AIDS and trafficking in women are all increasing.  The labor force is being depleted, as large numbers of Moldovans are becoming economic migrants. On the eve of the first year of the new millennium, the Government is launching a strategy for poverty alleviation in the face of declining standards of living, slow growth and high unemployment.
UNDAF Rationale.  The rationale for this common framework for UN assistance to Moldova has three pillars.
First, given the size and complexity of the problems described above, the UN system, with its limited resources, must develop a strategic and coordinated approach in order to optimize its impact.  In the context of the needs and priorities of the country, this approach will concentrate UN system resources in key areas and enable systematic intervention in accordance with the comparative advantages and mandates of UN Agencies.
Second, the UN system lacks the resources to address all of the problems identified in the Common Country Assessment.  Thus, as a statement of the priorities of the UN system for Moldova, the UNDAF will also serve as a tool for resource mobilization and a frame of reference for cost sharing, joint programming or parallel financing with other development partners.
Third, many issues confronting Moldova are directly related to the action agendas of the UN global conferences.  Moldova participated in these conferences and has ratified related conventions and agreements.  The Government is mandated to implement these action agendas and agreements and UN Agencies are required to monitor and report on implementation.  In line with this, the UNDAF states conference follow-up to be one of the priorities of the UN cooperation with the country and integrates it into the approaches of the UN system to Moldova’s development needs and problems.
II.	Goals and Objectives
Objectives of the Government  
The ongoing Action Program of the Government of the Republic of Moldova has five objectives:
“strengthening of state institutions to ensure further democratization of society, law supremacy, constitutional rights and obligations of all citizens, enhancing the efficiency of public administration and combating corruption and organized crime;
raising the level of social responsibility of the state in order to support socially vulnerable categories of the population, to reform the social sector and to reduce unemployment and poverty;
placing major emphasis on the real sector of the economy using mechanisms of encouraging the economic agents, accelerating the structural reform process, supporting and protecting entrepreneurs and improving corporate management of enterprises by means of creating favorable conditions for investments and exports;
promoting activities aimed at settling the Transnistrian issue and ensuring the integrity of the Republic of Moldova;
improving the image of the Republic of Moldova abroad as a reliable political and economic partner and integration into international and regional structures, taking into account the interests of the country and national security interests.”
Goals of the UN System.
The goals of development assistance to be provided from the UN system cover three broad areas to support the Government Action Program. These goals seek to achieve the following results:
A vibrant market economy that will create sustainable livelihoods;
Governance that is effective and accountable at both the central and local levels;
Social services in health, education and social welfare that are provided effectively and fairly to meet the needs of the general population and of vulnerable groups in particular.
Cross-cutting Objectives
In the design and implementation of its operational strategies, the UN system will integrate and further the achievement of four objectives that cut across all three goals, namely:
1.  The Alleviation of Poverty.  Pursuant to the World Summit for Social Development (Copenhagen, 1995) and with advice and support from the IMF, the World Bank and UNDP, the Government has prepared an “Interim Poverty Reduction Strategy” in consultation with representatives of the Parliament, civil society organizations and the donor community.  The strategy has three goals: (i) sustainable and inclusive economic growth; (ii) increased access to basic services, especially health care and primary education; (iii) social protection policies for those most in need.  The alleviation of poverty is a key dimension of the UNDAF strategy in the areas of economic growth and social sector reform and development. A recent assessment of poverty in Moldova identified families with many children, pensioners, and landless peasants as the poorest groups in the population.  These groups as well as other vulnerable groups are the targets of many UNDAF activities.
2.  Sustainable Development.  With support from UNDP, the Government has developed the National Strategy for Sustainable Development (Moldova 21) in accordance with Agenda 21 of the UN Conference on Environment and Development (Rio de Janeiro, 1992). As a follow up to this initiative, a project has been developed for the elaboration of local Agenda 21 envisaging, among others, support for the National Sustainable Development Commission and the pilot development of local level sustainable development plans. Sustainable development concerns are also integrated, for example, into the UNDAF activities in the areas of agriculture, industry and power. The implementation of national obligations under international environmental conventions is a component within the governance area.
3. Gender Equality.  The Government of Moldova has actively undertaken measures to implement the Plan of Action adopted at the Fourth World Conference on Women (Beijing, 1995).  Specific gender issues are included in the UNDAF strategies in the areas of governance and social sector reform and development.
4. Promotion of Human Rights.  The Government has ratified the six main United Nations covenants on human rights that deal with, inter alia, cultural rights, political rights, racial discrimination, discrimination against women, inhuman treatment, and the rights of children.  To follow-up on the decisions of the World Conference on Human Rights (Vienna, 1993), the Government has created with the support of UNDP and UNHCHR the Center for Human Rights, which takes the lead in the promotion and protection of human rights in Moldova. All UN system Agencies integrate human rights concerns into their programmes. Human rights issues are reflected in the UNDAF strategy in the areas of governance and social sector reform and development.
Objectives of Assistance from the UN System
One objective for assistance from the UN system is set out below for each goal. The achievement of each objective will require interventions in a number of areas, most of which are not fully funded. The actual indicators for achievement will be established in these areas by the concerned UN Agencies during programming.  For each objective, the areas for operational activities are listed and generic types of indicators for achievement are proposed for use by the concerned UN Agencies.  
Objective 1:  Economic Growth and Reform.  The UN system will provide advice to the Government and strengthen its capacity to implement appropriate policies and programmes for sustainable economic growth and stability, further reform of the economy, job creation, and the promotion of trade, investment and regional economic cooperation.

Objective 2:  Governance.  The UN system will advise the Government, strengthen its capacity to develop appropriate policies and support the implementation of concrete programmes aimed at the implementation of the public sector reform, increasing capacities of local administrations to manage development processes at the local level, strengthening the judiciary, promotion of human rights and the implementation of conventions and laws that Moldova ratified over the years of independence. The UN system will also provide direct support to refugees and internally displaced persons in Moldova, promote the culture of peace, and facilitate the development of civil society.

The UN system will advise the Government and strengthen its capacity to develop and implement policies and programmes for reform and restructuring in education and culture, health, and services for vulnerable groups. The UN system will also support the development and strengthening of the data collection and analysis in the priority areas.

Cooperation Strategies and On-Going/Planned Activities in Priority Areas
The cooperation strategies of individual UN Agencies include advocacy; policy advice; the creation, development or transformation of institutional capacity; provision of the investment and balance of payments loans; and in some cases, direct support for the provision of essential services. 
As for the strategies for cooperation among UN Agencies, these include UN system-wide advocacy, joint and coordinated programming, information sharing, and the promotion of partnerships with other development partners and civil society organizations.
On-going and planned activities are presented by objective. For each objective an overview table is presented that lists the areas of intervention, the UN Agencies that are providing/plan to provide assistance in that area, and the development agencies that are also active in the area.
Cooperation on Economic Growth and Reform 
Table 4 provides an overview of ongoing and planned assistance from UN Agencies to Moldova in the area of economic growth and reform.
Table 4. Economic Growth and Reform
Participation of UN Agencies and Other Key Development Agencies
Macro-economic, fiscal, and monetary policies.  The International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank (WB) are the primary providers of advice to the Government on macro-economic, fiscal and monetary policies.  The implementation of their policy recommendations is a condition for the receipt of loans from these international financial institutions.  The IMF provides technical advice and capacity building assistance in a number of areas including fiscal management, public expenditure, monetary policy, central bank organization, and statistics.  The World Bank undertakes economic and sectoral research on Moldova as the basis for policy dialogue and provides loans for structural adjustment.  Both organizations provide overseas training for Moldovan officials at their respective training institutes.  
The promotion of sustainable and inclusive economic growth is one of the main goals of the Government’s poverty reduction strategy.  Both the IMF and the World Bank are focusing their policy advice and lending programmes for the coming years on the implementation of this strategy.  The IMF will provide a $150 million loan, the “Poverty Reduction and Growth Facility”, for balance of payments support on highly concessional terms.  The World Bank is preparing its country strategy that will also focus new lending on poverty reduction.  
Banking sector reform and development.  The IMF is the lead international agency for the implementation of banking sector reform.  Working through the National Bank of Moldova, the IMF provides and will continue providing policy advice and technical assistance on bank supervision, foreign exchange operations and accounting.  IFAD also renders some support for banking sector reform through its Rural Finance and Small Enterprise Development Project. UPU could be implementing a project on the development of Postal Banking and Savings Services.
Privatization and promotion of foreign direct investment.  The World Bank and UNDP provide assistance in this area to deepen economic reforms and stimulate economic growth.  The World Bank undertakes analytical work on the environment for foreign investment in Moldova and general reviews of the private sector.  Through its IFC subsidiary, two loans are being disbursed for projects that provide funding for post-privatization restructuring and modernization, new joint ventures, and training and market information for local enterprise managers. Several donors and development agencies are also participating in these projects with the World Bank including the Governments of Germany, Japan and the Netherlands and EU/TACIS, GTZ and USAID. An IFC credit for telecommunications includes three private sector co-financing partners. In 1998, UNDP supported the establishment of the Moldova Foreign Investment Agency and is now considering the provision of additional capacity building for this agency. Investment and enterprise development, including the investment policy reviews and formulation of policy frameworks for attracting foreign investment, also makes part of the technical cooperation programme of UNCTAD.
Sustainable development of agriculture and industry.  The World Bank undertakes regular analysis of the industrial and agricultural sectors as the basis for dialogue on sectoral policies.  It has provided loans for key projects to upgrade electricity production, with technical assistance from USAID. In addition, it lends to build capacities for agricultural research and the provision of agricultural support services.  
FAO, which sponsored a workshop in Moldova to follow up on the decisions of the World Food Summit (Rome, 1996) and stimulate a national dialogue on a strategy for agricultural development, will conduct its country strategy exercise for the country in early 2001.  This strategy will set the parameters for future FAO cooperation in Moldova, with the specific areas of intervention being product quality in agricultural production and food processing, training and capacity building in market economy environment and institution building, and sustainable management of water resources for agriculture. 
IAEA plans to formulate a policy regarding the environmentally friendly nuclear technologies in agriculture to increase productivity and quality of production and the preservation of fruits and vegetables. UNIDO is also working on sustainable development issues. It is implementing a project on industrial energy efficiency and has developed a number of new proposals on energy conservation and the use of renewable energy resources. UNDP is administering a GEF-funded project on recycling of industrial refrigerants. Finally, WIPO is working with the State Agency on Industrial Property Protection and the State Copyright Agency of Moldova on the development of an effective national intellectual property protection system including the enforcement of the industrial property rights. One of the future plans is to develop a framework programme of cooperation between Moldova and WIPO that would cover all aspects related to intellectual property.
Income generating activities.  Income generating activities sponsored by the UN system are targeted for low-income households in order to alleviate poverty.  The World Bank and IFAD are both funding rural credit schemes to provide Moldovan farmers with resources to expand their production capacities. IFAD’s project is being supplemented by a grant from CNFA/USAID. Also participating in the Bank Rural Finance Project are the Government of the Netherlands, GTZ and the Soros Foundation. Another World Bank loan project, the Social Investment Fund, provides funding for short-term employment on rural public works and for micro-business development. Other agencies participating in this project include the Governments of Sweden and Japan, the Soros Foundation and USAID.  UNDP and UNCHS have prepared an urban development project proposal that includes a component for income generating activities. This component will provide training and funding for unskilled workers to undertake environmental rehabilitation in urban areas.  Finally, UNHCR is assisting refugees and asylum seekers to become economically self-sufficient.
Trade and regional economic cooperation.   Moldova’s application for membership in the World Trade Organization (WTO) is pending final review and approval. In anticipation of this, the International Trade Center (ITC) has prepared a foreign trade promotion project, which aims at facilitating the economic development of the country through the expansion of export earnings. ITC will also continue providing support to the Moldovan Association of Supply Managers established in the framework of one of its projects. UNCTAD that, together with UNDP, implemented a project on Debt Management might be rendering technical assistance to Moldova in such areas as trade policy formulation, development of the trade-related financial services infrastructure and facilitation of trade efficiency. 
ECE has been providing assistance in the development of marketing of non-wood forest products in countries in transition. In the coming years, being a member of the Black Sea Economic Cooperation (BSEC), Central European Initiative (CEI), Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) and Southeast European Cooperative Initiative (SECI), Moldova will continue benefiting from the ECE substantial involvement in all operational activities/projects undertaken in cooperation with these subregional groupings. 
UNDP Resident Representatives in the region have been informally discussing arrangements for regional economic cooperation between Moldova, Ukraine and Romania.  Assistance from the UNDP Regional Bureau for Europe may be requested for the development of a regional project.
Facilitating Moldova’s integration into the European Community might also be one of the focus areas for the UN assistance in the future, although further consultations with the Government will be required in this field.
Infrastructure for development.  World Bank will continue to provide loans for infrastructure development projects, with increasing emphasis on investments that will contribute directly to poverty alleviation. UNCHS and the World Tourism Organization are developing projects to plan infrastructure development for urban areas and tourist facilities, respectively. The UNCHS/UNDP proposal is directly derivative of the action plan adopted at the UN Conference on Human Settlements (Istanbul, 1996) that called for the strengthening of management mechanisms for sustainable human settlements. The project includes poverty alleviation activities, environmental rehabilitation and the promotion of environmentally sound construction technologies. IAEA will fund a project on the development of a facility for radioactive waste processing and storage as well as will work on the creation of the system for the effective national radioactivity monitoring. ITU will continue providing assistance for human resources development in the telecommunications sector. UPU may participate in reform and development in the postal sector, one of the plans being the establishment of public access Internet points at post offices in different parts of the country as a way to promote local social and economic development. WMO is supporting the implementation of a regional project focused on the provision of specialized hydro meteorological information and services to a new transport corridor Europe-Caucasus Asia. In 2001, work will be started on one more four-year regional project on the development of the hydrological services in the Black Sea region, in which Moldova will also take part. One more important area of the UN work during 2001-2005 will be the promotion of information and communication technologies. UNDP, the World Bank and the Government have already signed a memorandum of understanding to work together to establish Moldova’s presence on the Internet, a “Moldova Gateway”, focusing on development issues and will continue working in this field. UNESCO expressed readiness to field a mission in 2001 to assess the current situation in the communication and information Sector and prepare project proposals to be implemented during 2001-2005.
Opportunities for enhancing collaboration within the UN system and with key development partners on economic growth and reform.  Within the UN system and with other development partners, a promising opportunity exists for sharing information and coordination in regard to income generating activities. Sharing of information on strategies, target populations, operational methods, and successes and failures could greatly assistance in the coordination of complementary efforts, standardization or harmonization of terms for micro-credit and refinement of operations based on successful models.
The large volume of assistance provided in the general area of private sector development, including privatization, trade and investment promotion also suggest another area for possible collaboration, at least for systematic sharing of information.  The very practical work of the EBRD deserves consideration as a model for assistance for private sector development.
Cooperation on Governance
Table 5 provides an overview of ongoing and planned assistance from UN Agencies to Moldova in the area of governance.
Table 5. Governance
Participation of UN Agencies and Other Key Development Agencies
Public sector reform.  The World Bank is the only UN agency active in this area. It has a project under preparation that aims to build a market-oriented public administration and to establish an effective system for planning and management of Government resources. 
Decentralization and strengthening of local government.  The World Bank’s Social Investment Fund project has a component for the development of municipal and community capacity for rehabilitation of social infrastructure and improvement of delivery of social services. UNDP has been providing technical assistance for the restructuring and reform of local government that includes training in modern public administration methods and regional development planning.  Two new project proposals will also have components for strengthening local government.  The “Moldova 21” project will introduce sustainable development concepts, including sound environmental policies and technologies, into local government planning and operations.  The “Beautiful Moldova” project is a response to the UN Conference on Human Settlements (Istanbul, 1996). It incorporates recommendations of the UNCHS document, “Improvement in Urban Management”.  A component of this project will train officials of the Chisinau city and selected local governments in the participatory preparation of general development plans for urban areas.  This project is actively seeking cost-sharing partners.  UNICEF plans to strengthen local government capacity to provide community level services for the protection and development of children – particularly for children with special needs - adolescents and families and for mother and child health.  In effected areas, UNHCR provides orientation for local officials on the processing and rights of refugees and internally displaced persons.
Gender issues in governance.  In line with its mandate to support Moldova’s development into a stable and secure democracy, UNDP provided funding for the creation of the gender-sensitive Leadership School, where Moldovan managers, politicians, leaders of youth organizations, NGOs and private businesses have been trained in leadership theory and practices.  The School builds on the achievements of the previously implemented initiatives funded by Sida, “Development of Women’s Leadership and Networking” and “Gender-Sensitive Leadership, Competence and Networking in Politics” that supported women-politicians at the local level. Also, UNIFEM and UNDP are implementing projects to raise public awareness on two sensitive gender and human rights issues:  trafficking in women and violence against women. In particular, UNIFEM is funding a project with the Women’s Organization of Moldova to collect and disseminate information on trafficking in women and on violence against women to government officials, mass media and other civil society organizations.  UNDP, using a grant from the Government of the United States of America, is supporting the establishment of an NGO -- the Center for the Prevention of Trafficking in Women.  Supporting these and other efforts aimed at the effective implementation of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women will continue being a priority for the future.
Combating corruption and drug trafficking.  UNDP, in cooperation with the World Bank and other donors, is developing a project to elaborate a comprehensive anti-corruption programme for the Government, incorporating legal, institutional, economic and administrative components.  UNDP is preparing two project proposals related to illicit drugs:  a project on drug use prevention for possible funding by Sida and a regional project on drug trafficking for possible funding by the EU. UNDCP cooperates with Moldova through its regional project focusing on the provision of capacity building assistance to drug abuse treatment providers. As a result of these efforts, the demand for drugs in Eastern Europe is expected to be reduced and the projected spread of AIDS to be slowed. UNESCO plans to work on the promotion of online governance as a way to support democracy and transparency in the government decision-making, thus contributing to reducing corruption. Both corruption and drug trafficking impoverish the people of Moldova.  Addressing these issues is an essential element of the poverty reduction strategy.
Implementation of environmental conventions and laws.  Since 1993, the Government has signed 16 international environmental conventions and agreements.  With support from the UN system, follow-up action is underway on the Convention for Biodiversity, the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, the Montreal Protocol and several other agreements.  These ongoing and planned actions include:
Technical assistance and capacity building support for the National Programme for the Recovery and Recycling of Refrigerants with funding from the Global Environmental Facility (GEF), UNEP and UNDP;
Technical assistance and capacity building support for the implementation of the Government’s Biodiversity Strategy with funding expected from GEF. The World Bank is administering a GEF grant for development of the strategy.  Two projects are planned for GEF funding and UNDP implementation, one on biodiversity conservation and the other on forestry conservation and expansion of forest reserves;
Support to the preparations for the Rio follow-up summit – Rio plus 10 – in 2002, in the framework of the UNDP Local Agenda 21 project;  
Support by WHO for the development of the National Environmental Health Action Plan prepared by the Government in accordance with the Helsinki Declaration of Action on Environment and Health in Europe
Other areas that require interventions by the UN include the promotion of the environment-friendly technologies and production processes; harmonization of the national environmental legislation to European standards; use of renewable energy resources; and assessment of the desertification processes in Moldova. Also, since Agenda 21 stressed the need to make environmental and trade policies mutually supportive, appropriate national actions might be initiated with the support from UNCTAD. The initiation of specific programmes and projects in the above areas will be subject to the mobilization of necessary funding.  
Judicial reform.  UNDP is already implementing the second phase of assistance to further strengthen the judicial system.  This phase will provide technical assistance for institutional development of the judiciary and advice on legal, management and operational issues.
 Promotion of human rights.  Moldova has ratified six international conventions and covenants on human rights that deal with, inter alia, cultural rights, political rights, racial discrimination, discrimination against women, inhuman treatment, and the rights of the child. The latter Convention was ratified in 1990 and UNICEF will follow up with the Government on its obligation to provide progress reports to the UN Committee on the Rights of the Child. Regarding the two covenants dealing with stateless persons and one on refugees, these have not yet been ratified by the country.  UNHCR will advocate accession to these treaties with the Government and encourage the establishment of structures and procedures for asylum seekers and refugees in the context of irregular migration. . 
Moldova participated in the World Conference on Human Rights (Vienna, 1993). Conference participants agreed to create and promote action plans for the protection of human rights.  In response to the Vienna Conference, UNHCHR and UNDP provided support for the establishment of a Center for Human Rights in Moldova under the jurisdiction of the Parliament.  The Center was established in 1998 and additional assistance in being provided to strengthen its capacity to promote and protect human rights in accordance with these international conventions and the constitution of Moldova.  
Promotion of civil society organizations.  Many civil society organizations in Moldova are focusing on the crosscutting issues being addressed by the UN system: poverty, environment, gender and human rights. UN system Agencies promote civil society organizations in Moldova in several ways:  by consulting them in the course of strategy and programme formulation, by using them as implementing agencies, by fostering complementary relationships between civil society organizations and Government, and, in some cases, by directly supporting the establishment of new civil society organizations.  The World Bank, UNDP, UNHCR and UNICEF invite civil society organizations to provide input into the design and implementation of their programmes and projects. In the course of such deliberations, UN system Agencies seek to foster complementary and appropriate relationships among civil society organizations and Government agencies that work in the same area.  The Bank, UNDP, UNICEF, UNFPA, and UNHCR all use civil society organizations (or non-governmental organizations) as implementing agencies for their activities.  For example, World Bank lending to the Moldova Rural Finance Corporation is extended to 185 community-owned savings and credit associations for on-lending to farmers.  UNHCR uses seven international and local non-government organizations to deliver much of its assistance.  The World Bank, UNDP and UNFPA have also directly supported the establishment of new civil society organizations.  The Bank and UNDP funded the establishment of the Center for Strategic Studies and Reforms as a non-government think tank.  This Center now provides contract research services to the UN system, such as the preparation of the Common Country Assessment and the National Human Development Report. UNFPA is supporting the establishment of family planning centers. Finally, some UN Agencies, e.g. the World Bank and UNEP, provide grants to NGOs to support their activities.
Promotion of the culture of peace and conflict mitigation.  The UN system regards Moldova as one country and its activities to promote the culture of peace, social cohesion and mitigation of the Transnistrian conflict all aim to strengthen national unity. The year 2000 was designated by the United Nations as the International Year for the Culture of Peace.  The National Commission for UNESCO and the UN Theme Group on Culture for Development with financial support from the Office of the UN Resident Coordinator launched a culture for peace movement in Moldova emphasizing the importance of non-violent resolution of the country’s numerous social, political, linguistic and regional tensions and conflicts. Pursuant to the agreement at the Millennium Summit, the UN system will continue to promote the culture of peace movement. In a related activity, UNDP is planning a project entitled, “Language as a Tool for Social Cohesion”, that will promote the national language as a social integration tool.  
In regard to the Transnistrian conflict, UNHCR is providing indirect support to internally displaced persons. UNDP is implementing a project in “popular diplomacy”, confidence-building exchanges between civil society organizations of both sides of the Nistru River.
Opportunities for enhancing collaboration within the UN system and with key development partners on governance.  UN system interventions in decentralization and strengthening of local government are piecemeal efforts.  Some consultation and collaboration among all actors in this area could produce an overall strategy that would integrate the concerns of all agencies and reduce the competition among agencies for the attention of local government officials.  
In regard to gender issues, the UN system institutional and funding bases are too narrow for approaching these sensitive and important issues. A wider forum with more resources might be created by elevating these issues for consideration by a broadly based group including the World Bank, UNICEF, UNDP and UNFPA and other interested development partners and civil society organizations. A similar recommendation can be made in the area of corruption and drug trafficking.
Cooperation on Social Sector Reform and Development 
Table 6 provides an overview of ongoing and planned assistance from UN Agencies to Moldova in social sector reform and development.
Table 6. Social Sector Reform and Development
Participation of UN Agencies and Other Key Development Agencies
Education and culture.  UN system support for education emphasizes the educational needs of younger children.  The World Bank, with additional support from the Governments of Japan and the Netherlands, is disbursing funds for an ongoing loan project to support general education development including the development and testing of new curricula, teaching materials, textbooks, teaching methods, and teacher training.  UNICEF’s country strategy includes the expansion of Early Child Care and Development practices from pilot kindergartens to the entire preschool system. The UNESCO Commission in Moldova has identified translation of textbooks into Romanian, access to education and libraries and the free flow of information in education, science and culture as key areas of need in the education sector, but at present, funding for assistance in these areas has not been identified.  In the future, the UN system will continue paying special attention to the problems in the education sector with a view to developing a long-term strategy for rehabilitation and development of the educational system. 
In regard to culture, UNDP plans to support the promotion of the national language under the “Language as a Tool of Social Cohesion” project.  The UNESCO Commission in Moldova will follow up with the Government concerning the ratification of the international convention on cultural heritage, which could facilitate fund raising for preservation and restoration of national treasures. UNESCO will also provide some funds to promote Moldovan arts and literature as well as carry out advocacy and public awareness activities related to cultural policy and cultural activities. Some funding for these was raised by the UN Theme Group on Culture from UNICEF, UNDP, the Soros Foundation and McDonald’s Corporation.
Health.  The World Bank has recently approved a credit and a technical assistance grant for the public health sector.  The project will fund development of the capacity to deliver health services with particular emphasis on providing access to essential services to the poor and on reducing the incidence of tuberculosis and HIV/AIDS.  
WHO provides technical assistance and training to Moldova in the context of its country programme which sets the framework for WHO technical assistance in six areas:  health policy development, health care reform, health of women and children, communicable diseases, non-communicable diseases and health promotion, and environment and health.  
UNICEF’s programme strategy for Moldova for 2002-06 continues to emphasize implementation of the agenda set by the World Summit for Children (New York, 1990) to meet the health needs of mothers and children.  This strategy includes policy dialogue on planning and implementation of mother and child health and adolescent health services; development of capacity of the Ministry of Health and local health services to deliver mother and child health services in the context of an effective and accessible public health care system; development of capacity to deliver adolescent health services, with particular emphasis on HIV/AIDS prevention.  
UNFPA provides assistance to Moldova, based on the recommendations of the Conference on Population and Development (Cairo, 1994), emphasizing advocacy and development of capacity for the delivery of reproductive health services that place emphasis on services for adolescents and prevention of sexually transmitted diseases and HIV/AIDS.
IAEA will be working on upgrading the efficiency of the External Beam Therapy of Oncological Patients as well as explore opportunities for cooperation in such areas as establishment of the national cancer registry and utilization of radioisotopes in diagnosis and therapy.
The UN Theme Group on HIV/AIDS, with support from UNAIDS, UNDP, UNICEF, UNHCR, WHO, the World Bank and several other donors, has developed an integrated multi-sectoral Action Plan for HIV/AIDS and will be working on its implementation.  In the health sector, this plan includes advocacy and public awareness activities and development of capacities for clinical care, HIV/AIDS testing and surveillance of the disease.  
Services for vulnerable groups.  A World Bank credit, with additional funding from the Government of Japan, is funding reform of the public pension system and providing financial support for the new organizational structure for social insurance. This credit addresses some of the needs of a major vulnerable group, namely, pensioners.  UNICEF will focus attention on special needs of children and adolescents who have been or are living in institutions. UNICEF will address de-institutionalization policy, reform of residential institutions, and the development of capacities in communities and civil society organizations to provide alternative living arrangements for children who are now in institutions. UNHCR provides direct support and services to refugees and internally displaced persons and assists health and educational institutions.  The integrated plan of action on HIV/AIDS includes development of local level action plans, related training of local authorities, and support for non-medical treatment of persons infected with HIV/AIDS. All UN Agencies support the principle of non-discrimination in the delivery of services to vulnerable groups.
Data collection and analysis.  UNDP funds and arranges the preparation of the National Human Development Report for Moldova.  This Report, which was prepared by the UNDP/WB Center for Strategic Studies and Reforms, with ILO support, during the last two years, aggregates and interprets basic HD indicators and analyses human development trends in Moldova.  UNICEF supports survey research and analysis in a number of areas including the accessibility of health services, household health expenditures, reproductive health, infectious diseases, and nutrition and food intake.  The WHO programme envisages data collection and analysis of key health indicators.  ILO is supporting “The Enterprise Labor Flexibility Survey” implemented by the Department of Statistical and Sociological Analysis and provides technical advisory assistance in the collection and analysis of labor market information. Due to the increased migration of the Moldovan citizens to foreign labor markets and the complexity of the statistical analysis of the migration flows, the UN might support research in the respective area. 
The World Bank and UNDP have jointly sponsored the establishment of the Center for Strategic Studies and Reform to create a non-government organization capable of a high level of research, data collection and analysis.  UNDP is also supporting a project to develop national capacity to monitor poverty at the Ministry of Economy and Reforms and plans, subject to the availability of funds, to launch a capacity building project at the Department of Statistical Analysis and Sociology.
Opportunities for enhancing collaboration within the UN system and with key development partners on social sector reform and development. The education area appears to be woefully under-funded, given the magnitude of the problems in the sector.  The UN system will, thus, address the question of how education can be approached by the Government and its UN and non-UN development partners in a more systematic way to define long-term strategies to solve the fundamental problems in education.  
The UN Theme Group on HIV/AIDS is a successful model for the development of an integrated, multi-sectoral approach to this complex problem.  This Theme Group will continue to function to coordinate the implementation of the Action Plan. 
Follow-Up and Review
Programming.  Despite some successful efforts to coordinate the programming cycles of UN Agencies, there is still considerable variation among Agencies in the length of the programme period and the beginning year of the cycle.  Indeed, most Agencies have shorter programming cycles than the five-year UNDAF period.  Furthermore, the lag between programming and implementation means that many programmes from the previous cycle will be prominent in the current UNDAF period.  While this situation applies to all UN Agencies, it is particularly true for the international financial institutions whose project loans are often drawn down over many years.  
Nevertheless, many UN agency strategy preparation or revision exercises are planned for the near future and the UNDAF provides a useful common frame of reference for programming by individual Agencies in accordance with their mandates. 
More to the point, the UNDAF identifies opportunities for new or enhanced collaboration that will be considered as Agencies prepare and revise their programmes and projects.
Policy dialogue and aid coordination.  The UNDAF will be used by the UN Resident Coordinator and by each UN agency, as appropriate, in policy dialogue with the Government, particularly in regard to the fulfillment of international commitments of the Government under global conventions and agreements and follow-up to global conferences sponsored by the United Nations.
The UNDAF will be used to guide the UN Resident Coordinator in the coordination of activities of the UN system.  In addition to the Development Cooperation Report funded by the Office of the Resident Coordinator, the UNDAF also provides useful information for donor coordination and assists in identification of opportunities for cooperation with key development agencies.  Finally, the Government may find the UNDAF to be helpful in its overall management of aid coordination.
Collaboration mechanisms.  The Resident Coordinator and UN Agencies will establish appropriate mechanisms for collaboration on the basis of consensus as needs arise.  There are two categories of arrangements for collaboration:  coordinating mechanisms and cooperation mechanisms. Coordinating mechanisms include inter alia the UN agency heads meetings, theme groups, and networking arrangements to coordinate policy and share information.  The status of the existing theme groups will be reviewed and consideration will be given to the desirability of setting up new groups or arrangements corresponding to the three objectives of the UNDAF or in the area of poverty alleviation.   Cooperation mechanisms could include arrangements for any joint programming among UN Agencies, management or steering committees for jointly implemented activities, or ad hoc task-based working groups on specific activities.  For all such mechanisms, the interested UN Agencies will prepare terms of reference in a consultative manner that are results-oriented, clearly linked to the UNDAF framework and possibly time-bound.
Resource mobilization.  The UNDAF and the Common Country Assessment identify areas of need that greatly exceed the resources available to the UN system.  The UNDAF and the CCA will be used by the Resident Coordinator and individual UN Agencies as baseline documents that define the priorities and strategies of the UN system for assistance to Moldova in discussions with bi-lateral donors and other potential partners for possible parallel financing, joint programming or cost sharing.  
Each UN agency will use the UNDAF in its own resource mobilization efforts.  The strategy for resource mobilization should emphasize that the UNDAF has defined common goals for UN assistance in areas of the competencies and mandates of the UN Agencies working in Moldova.  Furthermore, it should be noted that UN Agencies have extensive operational experience in Moldova and strong relationships with Government agencies and CS organizations.  Finally, UN agency operations are planned and implemented at the request of Government in consultation with other development partners and the civil society.  Reporting on these activities by UN Agencies is open and transparent.
Monitoring and review.  Programmes and projects included in the UNDAF will be monitored, reviewed and evaluated by their respective UN sponsors.  These Agencies will be responsible for monitoring and evaluation, including the establishment of specific benchmarks and indicators, in accordance with their own procedures.  These UN agency monitoring and evaluation processes will provide the assessment data on the extent to which UNDAF objectives are being achieved.
The UN Resident Coordinator and UN Agency representatives will review the implementation of the UNDAF regularly in the course of the UN system coordination meetings.  The success of the UNDAF will be measured in terms on increased collaboration among UN system Agencies and Government response to the system-wide framework.
Finally, the Government will periodically review the implementation of the UNDAF and advise UN system Agencies of its findings and recommendations.
Programme Resources Framework
As per the instruction in the UNDAF Guidelines, the regular programme contributions of the international financial institutions are not included in the Programme Resources Framework table (see Annex 1) though their contributions are discussed in the text.  As a result, UN system resources devoted to economic growth and reform appear slight.  However, this is the main area for World Bank and IMF intervention.  Each of these agencies is currently providing $40-50 million of loans and technical assistance grants to Moldova annually.  
Similarly, the high level of contributions of UN Agencies to the social sector reflects the mandates of most of the Agencies that are currently active in Moldova:  UNICEF, UNFPA, UNHCR, UNAIDS and WHO.

Lessons Learned from UN System Cooperation in the Last Cycle
1. Follow up to Global Conferences. Although, as described in the CCA, quite a number of activities have been successfully implemented, these activities have been scattered and have had to do more with the work of individual UN Agencies than with the activity of the UN system as a unified force. 
2. Collaborative programming. The issue of developing and implementing joint programmes in Moldova has been discussed at length. Some attempts have even been made to initiate such programmes, e.g., the UNDP/WB project on the establishment of the Center for Strategic Studies and Reforms, UNDP/WB project on Poverty Alleviation Strategy, UNDP/UNHCHR project on the Human Rights Center.  
Another efficient form of inter-agency collaboration in Moldova consists of the implementation by individual UN Agencies of separate projects in one thematic area (e.g. private sector development or the social sector), with specific activities under these separate projects being coordinated. This form of co-operation has several clear advantages. 
First, this form of collaboration is easier to implement given that only two of the UN Agencies working in Moldova have fully harmonized programming cycles. When UN Agencies are passing though different stages of their programming cycles, often with core resources already fully allocated or spent, planning and implementation of new large-scale joint activities/programmes/projects is very difficult. 
Second, while the implementation of joint programmes proper would require the harmonization of certain administrative/operational/financial rules and procedures, the form of inter-agency co-operation described above gives each individual UN Agency an opportunity to follow its own rules for project or programme implementation. 
Third, this approach allows appropriate application of the diversity and specializations focuses of UN Agencies active in Moldova, with each agency concentrating on elements of multifaceted problems that correspond to its specific mandate.
The last but not least important issue of concern is that of resource mobilization. As resources of individual UN Agencies that are available for joint programming are rather scarce, resource mobilization acquires special importance. Unfortunately, as yet there have been no reliable mechanisms established for mobilizing funds for joint programmes/projects. 
3. Coordination/Cooperation Mechanisms.  The main three types of coordination/cooperation mechanisms used by the UN team in Moldova included: UN Agency Heads Meetings; operational committees of Programme, Administrative and Public Information Officers; and Theme Groups.  After several years of operation, it is clear that while the first type of coordination mechanism is crucial for reaching agreement on the important policy issues pertaining to UN cooperation in the country, the operational committees are responsible for putting these agreements into practice. Thus, it is important to maintain both types of coordination mechanisms in the future. 
Regarding the Theme Groups, the experience shows that these are most successful when there is a practical collaborative initiative that provides a “glue” for inter-agency cohesion; at least some seed funding is available for the initiation of the TG activities; there is no specific lead agency in the field, with all members of the UN Team sharing equal ownership of the Group and its results and being equally committed to making the Group a success. In such a case, UN Agencies are ready to dedicate the necessary amount of time and human resources to the Group, which is crucially important for its successful operation. Another clear lesson learnt is the more relevant non-UN partners that are involved in theme group work, the more efficient the group eventually becomes.  Theme Groups may also be successful when many UN Agencies, by virtue of their mandates, are involved in a specific field or if the “theme” of the TG relates to the cross-cutting, relevant for every UN Agency objectives. In such cases, one of the main tasks of the group may consist in the coordination of on-going efforts and information sharing. 
One rather new but successful form of inter-agency coordination is the establishment of ad hoc coordination groups charged with the fulfillment of very specific tasks (e.g. CCA/UNDAF Working Groups).  Such groups should be continued in the future as needed.
It is important that the participation of various Agencies in all the above-mentioned coordination groups and committees differs, which is directly related to the fact that some UN Agencies in Moldova have a very limited staff and cannot participate in every meeting. 
4. Cost-effectiveness of the operational activities for development.   During the past several years, a large number of common services have been developed. Such services should be expanded given that they clearly reduce the operational expenses of UN Agencies.
5. Small projects vs. big programmes. The development and implementation of comprehensive national programmes frequently require the initiation of larger technical assistance programmes rather then separate small-scale projects. Indeed, large programmes allow problems to be addressed in a more profound manner and provide a greater opportunity to achieve results. The initiation of more numerous medium and small-scale projects can, on the contrary, lead to the dissipation of resources, both human as well as monetary. Nonetheless the experience shows that small and middle-sized projects do have some advantages. These include: 
a) attractiveness for resource mobilization;
b) the capacity to address many priority areas simultaneously and in a flexible manner;
c) given the small size of Moldova, smaller projects that derive from and support the implementation of large national programmes can have an important impact and can build important capacity which permits them, in spite of their small size, to become sustainable.
